definition: Discharge planning is the process of organizing care as a patient leaves inpatient treatment. In this mental health context, it refers to a team-based, pharmacy-guided workflow designed to support ongoing treatment after discharge and help reduce readmission.

reasons: The packet only states that a “pharmacy-guided AUD discharge planning workflow” was studied for its impact on “MAT prescriptions and inpatient readmissions.” It does not support the broader statement that discharge planning is “the process of organizing care as a patient leaves inpatient treatment.”

The definition claims a “team-based” and “pharmacy-guided workflow” designed to support ongoing treatment after discharge; the packet mentions “pharmacy-guided” but does not provide support for “team-based,” “ongoing treatment after discharge,” or the general purpose described.

The definition says the workflow is intended to “help reduce readmission,” but the packet only indicates the study assessed readmissions; it does not explicitly support a claim about intended reduction (beyond measuring impact).
The definition frames the term as applying to a general “mental health context,” while the packet evidence is specific to alcohol use disorder (AUD).

The packet supports a specific alcohol-use-disorder discharge planning workflow, not the broad general definition of discharge planning as a general process of organizing care when a patient leaves inpatient treatment.
“Designed to support ongoing treatment after discharge” is not stated in the packet; the source only says the workflow was to affect MAT prescriptions and inpatient readmissions.
The term is presented as a team-based, pharmacy-guided workflow, but the definition adds broader clinical purpose and scope that are not fully supported by the source text.
